exposure: total weight gain greater than recommendation
cohort: Pregnant women with an abnormal 50-g glucose challenge test but without a diagnosis of gestational diabetes mellitus, who delivered between January 2018 and December 2020.
finding: Pregnant women with an abnormal 50-g GCT but without GDM had a higher risk of adverse neonatal outcomes, with specific risk factors identified for large-for-gestational-age infants, neonatal hypoglycemia, and respiratory distress syndrome.
mod_finding: Operative delivery was identified as a significant risk factor for neonatal hypoglycemia, and cesarean delivery was highly prevalent (46%) in this cohort.
gest_age: Gestational age at GCT was between 24 and 28 weeks; preterm birth was an identified risk factor and large-for-gestational-age infants were an outcome.
